label: Mirror fork for necessitarians; contrast gap of invariant sources (inference)
rule: Collapse with essence-grounded possibility identifies every unexcluded world with the actual one; case analysis on which premise of the mirror argument fails
meaning: Clause 1: under collapse, an unexcluded world is accessible and so satisfies 'is w'. Clauses 2-4 locate the necessitarian's exit: with reversal and the possibility principle, some essential truth separates w from σ w (a nature containing orientation, option 1); with preservation but without the possibility principle, σ w is unexcluded and impossible (brute, option 3); with the possibility principle and preservation, σ w = w and no feature is reversed (no distinct mirror image, option 2, which by clause 1 generalizes to every unexcluded world). Clause 5: a necessitating rule that singles out w is itself not mirror-invariant at w. Clause 6: for every source whose real determinations are invariant over accessible worlds (an impersonal propensity, or the classical root on the relation-of-reason account) no intrinsic fact discriminates this handedness from the other. Clause 7: an orientation token with a par alternative is excluded at an actual root by the requirement-form purity premises (the handedness instance of lane P's mechanism, proved from the declarations on main). The certificate does not favour personal over impersonal accounts; it presses necessitarian accounts of either kind and any claim that an invariant source's intrinsic profile explains the contrast.
